# COIN (Coinbase Global, Inc.) Technical Report, as of 2026-11-24

## 1. Data integrity

- The `get_verified_market_snapshot` values match the individual `get_indicators` outputs for 2026-11-24 (10 EMA 115.11, 50 SMA 160.74, 200 SMA 171.84, RSI 27.32, MACD -16.15, Bollinger middle 130.15, lower band 93.91, ATR 8.91). I found no conflicts.
- The Bollinger upper band (166.38), MACD signal (-14.26) and MACD histogram (-1.89) come only from the snapshot. I did not make separate calls for them.
- **Caveat on the latest bar:** the 2026-11-24 row shows Open = High = 107.49 and a volume of 7,164,719. That volume is not rounded to the hundreds like the other rows, so it may be a partial or in-progress session. I can't confirm this from the tools. If so, the close of 102.35, the volume and every indicator that uses them could still change.
- I did not retrieve VWMA, so I make no volume-weighted trend claims. Volume remarks below are raw observations from the OHLCV table.

## 2. Indicator set and rationale

| Indicator | Reason for inclusion |
|---|---|
| close_10_ema | Fast momentum and the nearest overhead resistance reference |
| close_50_sma | Medium-term trend and dynamic resistance |
| close_200_sma | Long-term trend benchmark and cross status |
| macd (with signal and histogram from the snapshot) | Trend momentum and its direction |
| rsi | Oversold or overbought state and divergence checks |
| boll and boll_lb (boll_ub from the snapshot) | Volatility envelope and mean-reversion reference levels |
| atr | Stop distance and position sizing |

The set is intentionally complementary: trend (three averages), momentum (MACD, RSI), volatility and range (Bollinger, ATR).

## 3. Price action

**Verified latest bar (2026-11-24):** open 107.49, high 107.49, low 101.91, close 102.35.

- **Magnitude of the decline.** The window peak close was 201.07 on 2026-09-22, with 201.05 on 09-21. The close of 102.35 on 11-24 is roughly 49% below that. Over the last month, the close fell from 160.59 on 10-29 to 102.35, about 36% lower.
- **Lowest levels in the six-month window.** The lowest close before the current leg was 142.52 on 06-25, and the lowest intraday low was 139.11 on 07-31. The current prices, with a 11-20 close of 101.97 and intraday lows of 101.71 (11-20) and 101.91 (11-24), are far below both.
- **Event-driven break.** On 10-30 the stock gapped from a 160.59 close to a 148.23 open and closed at 143.54. Volume was 20.89M, about 3x the typical 6–8M day, and it marked the start of the current leg down.
- **Persistent selling.** Closes were lower on most days from 11-12 to 11-20: 130.67, 127.65, 119.84, 115.02, 110.51, 108.87 and 101.97. Volume was elevated on 11-16 (11.23M) and 11-20 (14.19M).
- **Failed bounce.** On 11-23 the stock closed at 108.78 (+6.7% from 101.97) on 10.80M volume. On 11-24 the open of 107.49 was also the high, so the stock traded below its open all day and gave back most of the bounce by closing at 102.35. This is a bearish reaction, but the bar may be incomplete (see Section 1).
- **Retest of the low.** The intraday lows of 101.71 on 11-20 and 101.91 on 11-24 are very close together. I have no evidence that this zone has acted as support before. It is only a two-touch retest so far, not a confirmed floor.

## 4. Trend structure

| Level | Value | Close vs. level (computed) |
|---|---:|---|
| Close | 102.35 | |
| 10 EMA | 115.11 | close about 11% below |
| 50 SMA | 160.74 | close about 36% below |
| 200 SMA | 171.84 | close about 40% below |

- **Price is below all three averages.** The averages are stacked bearishly: 10 EMA < 50 SMA < 200 SMA.
- **A 50/200 death cross has occurred.** The 50 SMA was 176.47 versus a 200 SMA of 176.43 on 11-05. By 11-06 the 50 SMA was 175.35 versus 175.99, so the cross happened between those two dates. The gap on 11-24 is about 11 points (160.74 vs. 171.84) and has been widening. This is a lagging confirmation of a downtrend that is already well advanced, not a fresh timing signal.
- **The 10 EMA is falling every session:** 137.94 (11-13), 119.98 (11-20), 117.94 (11-23) and 115.11 (11-24). The 11-23 bounce did not reclaim it, and the stock did not come close.
- **Overhead resistance is falling, which matters for bounce targets.** The 10 EMA (115.11) and Bollinger middle (130.15) decline daily, so any bounce target moves lower the longer a rally is delayed. The 50 SMA has fallen from about 180 on 10-29 to 160.74, and the 200 SMA from about 179 to 171.84.

## 5. Momentum

**MACD**
- The MACD line is -16.15 against a signal of -14.26, so the histogram is -1.89. The MACD line is below the signal and well below zero.
- It deteriorated from -4.36 on 10-26 to -7.01 on 10-30 and -16.15 on 11-24. Over the last four sessions it has been flat to slightly worse (-15.89 on 11-20, -15.85 on 11-23, -16.15 on 11-24). Downside momentum has not clearly decelerated, and there is no bullish crossover.

**RSI**
- RSI is 27.32. It has been below 30 on every session from 11-16 to 11-24: 29.23, 27.44, 25.84, 25.26, 22.94, 29.80 and 27.32.
- The low was 22.94 on 11-20. RSI has since made a higher low at 27.32, while price closes are nearly equal (101.97 vs 102.35). That is **not** a true bullish divergence, which requires a lower price low. It is only a tentative sign that selling pressure per bar is easing, and MACD does not confirm it.
- A strongly trending decline can keep RSI oversold for extended periods. Oversold readings alone are not a buy signal here.

## 6. Volatility and Bollinger Bands

- **Bands:** lower 93.91, middle 130.15, upper 166.38. Width is about 72 points, which is very wide and reflects the heavy selling since 10-30.
- **Position in the bands:** the close of 102.35 is 8.44 points above the lower band, or about 12% of the way up the band range (computed). It is far below the middle band.
- **Band walk:** closes from 11-16 to 11-24 have stayed above the lower band without closing below it. For example, 11-20's close of 101.97 was above that day's lower band of 99.41. Price is hugging the lower band while the band itself falls. In strong trends this is typically a continuation pattern rather than a reversal signal.
- **ATR:** 8.91 on 11-24, down from a recent peak of 11.06 on 11-05. In percentage terms it is about 8.7% of the close, versus about 6.5% on 10-26 (10.40 on a 159.60 close, computed). Daily ranges are therefore larger relative to price than before the selloff.

**Risk-sizing illustration (not a recommendation):**
- 1.5 × ATR is about 13.4 points.
- 2 × ATR is about 17.8 points.
- A stop placed inside one ATR of entry is within typical daily noise.

## 7. Scenarios supported by the data

**Bearish continuation (the path of least resistance given current evidence)**
- Trigger: a decisive close below the 101.7–102 zone (the 11-20 and 11-24 intraday lows).
- Reference level: the lower Bollinger band at 93.91, which is itself drifting lower.
- Supporting evidence: price below all averages, a death cross, MACD below its signal and zero, failed 11-23 bounce, and elevated volume on down days.

**Oversold relief bounce**
- Evidence for: RSI under 30 for seven sessions, price near the lower band, and a nearly equal price low with a higher RSI low.
- Resistance in order: the 10 EMA at 115.11, then the Bollinger middle at 130.15. Both are falling.
- A reclaim of the 10 EMA, a MACD histogram turning up, and RSI back above 30 would be the first confirmations to look for. None are present now.

**Not supported by the tools:** any claim that 101–102 is proven support, any reversal call, and any price target beyond the indicator levels listed. I have not backtested any of these signals.

## 8. Takeaways for the decision-maker

1. The trend is decisively bearish on every trend measure. Short-term oversold readings do not change that.
2. Any bounce is a counter-trend trade into falling resistance at 115.11 and 130.15. Size it for ATR of about 9 points (about 8.7% of price), not for a calm tape.
3. The 11-24 bar may be incomplete, so wait for the final close before relying on the failed-bounce reading or on the retest of the 11-20 low.
4. Watch for a close below roughly 101.7, a MACD histogram turn, and RSI moving back above 30 with price holding above the 10 EMA.

| 10 EMA | 115.11 | Falling; price about 11% below; nearest resistance |
| 50 SMA | 160.74 | Falling; price about 36% below |
| 200 SMA | 171.84 | Falling; price about 40% below |
| 50/200 cross | 50 SMA moved below 200 SMA between 11-05 and 11-06 | Death cross; gap about 11 points |
| MACD / signal / histogram | -16.15 / -14.26 / -1.89 | Bearish; momentum not yet recovering |
| RSI | 27.32 (low 22.94 on 11-20) | Oversold; below 30 for 7 sessions; no confirmed divergence |
| Bollinger lower / middle / upper | 93.91 / 130.15 / 166.38 | Price near the lower band; band walk; wide bands |
| ATR | 8.91 (about 8.7% of price) | High relative volatility; wide stops needed |

| Bounce hurdles | 115.11, then 130.15 | Both falling daily |

One user argues the stock "can't sustain ATH with a crypto president", which makes the policy tailwind look exhausted.

- Bitcoin direction, since COIN trades as a high-beta crypto proxy.

- Technical downside levels that posters cite, in the $60s to $70s.
- Minor event: a $2.25M Dogecoin sweepstakes settlement received final approval. It is immaterial.
- Caveat: social posts after a big down day over-represent anger. Capitulation-style sentiment can sometimes coincide with a local low, but nothing here establishes that.

I would not own COIN here. At best, this is a counter-trend trade into falling resistance with reward-to-risk near 1:1 to the first target. If you want to trade the bounce, treat it as a small trade with a 1.5 to 2 ATR stop, not an investment.
